b1fc85fc3216c6d9: KUALA LUMPUR: Hosts Japan surged to the top of the Aichi-Nagoya Asian Games medal standings as of 12pm after claiming two gold medals on the opening morning, while Malaysia remained without a medal.
Japan lead with two gold and two bronze medals, ahead of China with one gold, four silver and one bronze.
Japan's first gold came through Takumi Hojo in the men's individual triathlon before their karate squad added another title.
Malaysia's only medal prospect, wushu exponent Danish Aizad, finished joint-seventh in the men's Changquan final after scoring 9.700 points.
He was just 0.020 points outside the bronze-medal position, with Indonesia's Seraf Naro Siregar taking third on 9.720.
As of 12pm, Malaysia are empty-handed as five Asean rivals get on the board.
Cambodia, Indonesia and Vietnam collected two bronzes each, while Myanmar and the Philippines had one bronze apiece.
Mandy Cebelle Chen will compete in the women's Taijiquan-Taijijian combined event in afternoon after scoring 9.706 points in the Taijiquan routine to sit joint-fifth.
The Taijijian routine is scheduled for 1.30pm Malaysian time.
ae4b088481f2391a: MANILA, Sept 20 — Six allegedly armed individuals were killed in a clash with Philippine army and police forces in the country’s southern Bangsamoro Autonomous Region in Mindanao yesterday, authorities said, reported Xinhua.
While serving an arrest warrant for a suspect charged with carnapping with homicide, government forces moved in, prompting the suspect and his companions to allegedly open fire on the troops.
The incident triggered an exchange of gunfire that left six gunmen dead, while authorities later recovered five rifles.
The clash prompted around 350 residents to temporarily evacuate their communities.

Meanwhile, in a separate incident, a 33-year-old man was shot dead yesterday evening while walking along a road in Valencia City, Bukidnon Province, in southern Philippines, according to local police.
Initial investigation showed that the incident occurred at approximately 7.00pm.
An unidentified suspect approached and shot the victim three times.
The investigation was underway, police said. — Bernama-Xinhua
5f72d8406940b26b: KUALA LUMPUR, Sept 20 — Former prime minister Datuk Seri Najib Razak says Malaysians who have offered to help pay the RM50 million fine required under his conditional royal pardon should not feel “burdened or obliged” to do so.
The statement from his lawyers comes as the Najib Razak Solidarity Fund set up by Umno to help him meet the payment reached RM1 million by 9.30am yesterday, less than a day after it was launched.

“While our client is deeply touched by these expressions of solidarity, he does not wish the Party, its members and supporters, or members of the public to feel burdened or obliged on his account,” Najib’s lawyers in the firm Messrs Shafee & Co said in a statement issued on his behalf.

The lawyers said Najib was grateful to those who had offered assistance towards meeting the condition imposed under his conditional pardon, but stressed that such support should be given “entirely of their own free will and according to their respective means”.
Umno secretary-general Datuk Asyraf Wajdi Dusuki said the fund collected RM165,645 within its first hour and RM634,562.02 within three hours, with many contributors giving RM10 or RM50.
Asyraf later announced that the fund had reached RM1 million and urged supporters to continue contributing, including donations of RM10.

The fund was launched after Umno president Datuk Seri Ahmad Zahid Hamidi said contributions were open to party leaders, members and supporters, as well as anyone wishing to show their support voluntarily.
Zahid also said the initiative would be carried out transparently and systematically while complying with all applicable regulations and laws.
The fundraising effort has drawn mixed reactions online, with some questioning the decision to raise money for Najib and whether such funds could instead help people facing financial hardship.

The Federal Territories Pardons Board granted Najib a conditional pardon on Friday, allowing him to serve the remainder of his SRC International sentence under house arrest until August 23, 2028, subject to payment of the RM50 million fine and other conditions.
The Attorney General has clarified that the conditional pardon applies only to the prison sentence imposed in the SRC International case.
a374999ff316c879: NAGOYA: Warnings of a typhoon partly explained why the Asian Games opening ceremony in Nagoya took place in front of thousands of empty seats, organisers said Sunday.
Saturday's gala at the 30,000-capacity stadium officially launched the continent's premier sporting event, with Japan's emperor and empress in attendance.
Fireworks brought the show to a rousing conclusion, but while parts of the arena were full, others were noticeably devoid of people.
Olympic Council of Asia director general Husain Al-Musallam said they had to keep one block empty because of the Games flame.
"This is one part," he told reporters, adding that more than 70 percent of tickets were sold.
That contrasted with an announcement at the Mizuho Park Athletic Stadium that said the ceremony was sold out.
"But maybe if you remember, it was a typhoon warning coming to Nagoya and at the last minute the typhoon shifted," Al-Musallam added.
"So the same question I've been asked, what happens if the typhoon is coming? That could affect the situation."
There was no rain during the ceremony and the storm, having days earlier shaped as a potential threat to the Games, made a greater impact in the Tokyo region.
There was heavy rain there on Sunday, where some Games events are being hosted – notably the swimming – with possible wet weather forecast for Nagoya later Sunday and Monday. --AFP
c730e2dbd86f0ab3: SINGAPORE: A steady nerve is crucial when keeping watch over hundreds of data centres worldwide, facilities essential to the frictionless online banking, messaging and AI services that society relies on.
Analysts sit surrounded by digital maps and dashboards at the Singapore command centre of US firm Digital Realty, a major global operator of the warehouse-like sites filled with whirring servers.
The goal is not simply to react when something breaks, but to detect warning signs, such as a sudden rise in temperature, early enough to prevent disruption.
Daniel Naing, 37, and his colleagues handle thousands of system alerts flagging signs of trouble each week.
"If I panic, my team members will panic. So even though inside I may be nervous, I cannot show it," he told AFP.
The command centre and its two sister hubs, in Europe and the United States, provide round-the-clock oversight of more than 300 data centres across six continents.
Digital Realty rents its server space to around 6,000 companies big and small, with power disruptions and equipment failure the most common issues faced.
There are also detailed protocols for earthquakes and typhoons, and an approaching storm thousands of kilometres away is enough to put the team on standby.
Booming demand for data centres is a political hot potato in many places, as tech companies race to develop artificial intelligence tools that require massive amounts of computing power.
But without them "nothing works" in our high-tech world, said Serene Nah, managing director and head of Asia Pacific at Digital Realty.
Data centres are essential infrastructure -- a matter "almost like national security", she said.
"We need to be up running all the time."
Nah said, however, that "our business is very misunderstood" and has little support from the public, who believe data centres emit "a lot of carbon or heat" or "use up a lot of water".
"Yet everyone's scrolling their phones every day," and for each swipe "the data needs to go somewhere".
The company is prioritising renewable energy such as solar panels and closed-loop server cooling systems that continuously recycle water, Nah said.
False positives
The vulnerabilities of the sector were highlighted this year, when data centres run by Amazon's cloud arm were struck during the Middle East war.
Data centres operate 24 hours a day, so Naing and his colleagues take the 7 am to 7 pm shift in Singapore before handing over to Europe.
Engineers must attend to an alert within minutes. The teams liaise with those on the ground and call on a global network of experts to help, while keeping clients updated.
Digital Realty is one of the biggest providers of data centre server space along with rivals like Equinix, also a US company.
Meanwhile tech giants from Microsoft to Alibaba are racing to build their own data centres to train and run AI models -- part of a global buildout costing trillions of dollars.
Digital Realty's Global Command Centre in Singapore is housed inside one of three data centres that the company runs in the city-state.
Most areas of the data centre, whose roof is lined with solar panels, are off-limits for security reasons.

But AFP was shown a room where rows of black server cabinets formed long, narrow corridors, with bundles of yellow cables running overhead and the computer servers' high-velocity fans emitting a soft hum.
AI is accelerating the growth and complexity of data centres, but for operations at the command centre, humans remain indispensable, said Terence Tang, head of the Asia Pacific global command centre.

"We still need human intervention to really look at whether or not those are genuine outages, genuine alerts and alarms, because sometimes AI or automation can give you false positives," Tang told AFP.
916781a99f0224b5: KUALA LUMPUR, Sept 20 — The proposed House Arrest Act is aimed at addressing prison overcrowding, particularly involving remand detainees, who make up a significant proportion of the prison population while awaiting trial.

Home Minister Datuk Seri Saifuddin Nasution Ismail stressed that the proposal was not new, saying he had mooted it as one of the Home Ministry’s (KDN) measures since 2024 to reduce prison overcrowding and ensure the country’s correctional system is managed more effectively.

“The concept we have been discussing from the outset is clear, namely that for remand detainees who meet the requirements, the court may consider placing them under house arrest with electronic monitoring until their trial.
“Serious criminal cases have already been identified for exclusion from this mechanism.

“We do not yet have an act or law on house arrest. Previously, I mooted introducing one specifically for remand detainees, as remand detainees are one of the causes of prison overcrowding,” he said in a video uploaded on his Facebook page today.
Saifuddin Nasution said prison inmates comprised those who had been convicted and were serving their sentences, as well as remand detainees whose court proceedings had yet to be completed.
He said remand detainees referred to individuals who had been charged but were either denied bail or unable to post bail, resulting in them being held in prison pending trial.

“So, this combination of convicted inmates and remand detainees contributes to prison overcrowding. For example, we currently have 41 prisons, but the prison population is 93,000. Our prison capacity is 75,000,” he said.
He said if the proposed law was passed, the court could consider placing eligible remand detainees under house arrest, with their movements monitored using electronic devices until their trial date.
Saifuddin Nasution said the Cabinet had also given in-principle approval for KDN to begin the process of drafting and tabling the House Arrest Act in Parliament.

“The original objective remains the same, namely to reduce prison overcrowding and ensure that the country’s correctional system can be managed more effectively. That is the original context and purpose of the House Arrest Act that we have been discussing from the outset.

“If the Bill is passed, we can release these remand detainees to their homes and equip them with modern devices to monitor their movements until their trial date. That is the original purpose we have been discussing,” he said. — Bernama
ec682b5d5421a59e: MOSCOW: A parliamentary election that President Vladimir Putin has cast as a test of support for Russia's war in Ukraine entered its third and final day on Sunday, with the ruling United Russia party expected to retain its dominance in a political system critics say does not tolerate dissent.

The State Duma vote, the first since Russia launched its full-scale war in Ukraine in February 2022, is likely to be presented by the Kremlin as evidence of public backing for Putin's policies and for the war, Europe's deadliest conflict since World War Two, now in its fifth year with no sign of ending soon.
Most anti-war candidates were barred from the ballot.

Those who did run from the liberal Yabloko party, which has polled in the single digits in recent years but hoped to tap into war fatigue, said they feared for their freedom after courts handed long jail terms to two senior party figures before the vote for comments about the conflict deemed illegal by authorities.
Discrediting the army or spreading what authorities regard as fake news are punishable by lengthy prison sentences.
The Kremlin says national unity and some censorship are necessary during what it calls its special military operation in Ukraine.
It casts the conflict as part of an existential struggle with a hostile West and says Ukrainian intelligence services and other enemies are stepping up efforts to stir unrest inside Russia.

Putin on Friday accused Ukraine of trying to interfere in the election, citing what he said was a Ukrainian strike on the home of an election official in the Russian-controlled part of Ukraine's Zaporizhzhia region that killed Elena Astanina, the official.
Reuters could not independently verify details of the attack and there was no immediate comment from Kyiv.
Russian electoral officials also said on Saturday that an online voting system in Moscow had come under cyberattack.
Kyiv, which has suspended elections under martial law, has dismissed the Russian vote as a "pseudo election."

Despite what most experts see as the election's predictable outcome, the NEST think-tank in Berlin, co-founded by Kremlin critic Mikhail Khodorkovsky, whom Russian authorities have designated "a foreign agent", said the vote could still produce awkward moments for the Kremlin at a time of economic strain.

"The consequences of the war are increasingly being felt within the country, and accumulated anxiety and frustration may translate into votes for the systemic opposition parties that the Kremlin has allowed to remain on the ballot," it said in a note.

It said the Communist party and the New People party could attract votes the authorities would prefer to go to United Russia. Both parties have consistently voted in line with United Russia on major issues.
Putin told the nation in a televised address before the election that the vote would underline support for Russian troops fighting in Ukraine.

"Your choice, and your will, will once again demonstrate that millions of people stand behind our soldiers, that we are a united people bound together by shared values, historical memory, and love for our homeland, and that no one will succeed in dividing or intimidating us," said Putin.
Initial results are expected to start emerging at around 1800 GMT on Sunday, with more complete results available on Monday.
b76fc4b11adffdd1: NILAI: Police are investigating a fight believed to have involved a staff member at the Labu KTM Komuter station and a passenger, following a viral video of the incident.
District police chief Superintendent Johari Yahya said police were also investigating the cause of the altercation and verifying when it actually occurred.
He said police detected the one-minute-36-second video, which showed two men involved in a fight at the station, circulating on TikTok around 3.45pm yesterday.
"Following this, a police report was lodged by the Labu police station chief at 4.26pm yesterday, and the case is being investigated under Section 160 of the Penal Code," he said in a statement.
Johari said investigations were ongoing to establish the cause of the fight, verify the actual date and time of the incident and determine the involvement of both individuals.
He advised the public against speculating or spreading unverified information, as this could interfere with investigations and cause public concern.
Those with information can contact the Nilai district police headquarters operations room at 06-790 4222 or any nearby police station.
According to the viral video, an elderly man had asked a staff member about a train delay but was allegedly given an unsatisfactory response.
A male passenger then confronted the staff member, resulting in the altercation.
Keretapi Tanah Melayu Bhd (KTMB) said it would also investigate the incident.
0e4c963615092719: KUALA LUMPUR: The national karate exponents have been told to adapt and leave no room for excuses after an early accommodation issue in Japan was swiftly resolved by team officials.
Upon arriving for the Aichi-Nagoya Asian Games, the national camp encountered a hiccup when there were insufficient hotel rooms available for the team.
However, quick intervention by the Olympic Council of Malaysia (OCM) and National Sports Council (NSC) ensured the matter was resolved without disrupting their final preparations.
National coach R. Sharmendran, a four-time SEA Games champion, said the team took the situation in its stride and commended the secretariat for their prompt support.
"There wasn't enough rooms when we first arrived, but we are grateful to OCM and NSC as they acted very fast to fix the problem," Sharmendran said to NSC's Kapsul.
"Food options around the hotel are also plentiful, so logistics are no longer an issue. The support from the secretariat has been solid."
Rather than allowing off-mat issues to become a distraction, Sharmendran challenged his exponents to treat the experience as a test of their mental strength.

"There is a saying that you have to compete at the highest level even in the worst conditions. Anything can happen or go wrong, but the objective remains the same, you still have to compete to win," he said.

"Instead of dwelling on what's happening around them, the athletes must focus entirely on what they can control. That means controlling their mindset, their discipline, and their performance on the tatami."
Karate has traditionally been one of Malaysia's medal-producing sports at the Asian Games, and the current squad will be looking to maintain that record.
At the previous Asian Games in Hangzhou, Malaysia won one gold and two silver medals.

Arif Afifuddin Malik captured the men's kumite under-84kg gold to end Malaysia's nine-year wait for a karate title at the Games, while Lovelly Anne Robberth won silver in the women's individual kata and another silver in the women's team kata.
Malaysia's best Asian Games haul in karate came at the 2010 Guangzhou edition, when the national team won two gold, two silver and one bronze.
The gold medals were secured by kata exponent Ku Jin Keat and kumite fighter R. Puvaneswaran.
cad7f9c5031b35c2: KUALA LUMPUR: Selangor coach Kim Pan Gon praised his charges for rediscovering their fighting "DNA" after Brazilian forward Chrigor Moraes netted a hat-trick in their 4-1 rout of Star City, but pulled no punches over the poor pitch conditions at the Tuanku Syed Putra Stadium.
The Red Giants produced a comeback in Kangar on Saturday to take a commanding three-goal advantage into the FA Cup quarter-final second leg at the MBPJ Stadium on Oct 10.

While delighted with his side's grit, Pan Gon stressed that the substandard playing surface posed a threat to player safety and contributed to Star City's opening goal after a Selangor player twisted his ankle on the uneven turf.
"The pitch condition was very, very disappointing," Pan Gon said.

"We cannot put our players in this kind of circumstance. We need to protect our players and protect the game. Our player twisted from nothing, just because of the surface, leaving us with fewer men on the pitch when we conceded.

"Anyhow, our players overcame all the difficult circumstances, an away game, the pitch condition, and high pressure. We want to get back our real Selangor DNA: mentally and physically strong, with a winning habit where we never give up."
Star City took the lead through Moses Atede in the 18th minute, but Moraes levelled three minutes later before Vitor Pernambuco put Selangor ahead in the 43rd.
Moraes completed his hat-trick with goals in the 61st and 87th minutes.
Despite holding a 4-1 advantage, Pan Gon warned his players against complacency ahead of the return clash.
"We will not be overconfident and we will not lose our concentration," he said.
"We will use this break period to review our performance, correct mistakes, and come back even stronger."

For Star City coach Mehmet Durakovic, the match slipped away after a spirited first-half display, with the former Selangor boss admitting that Pan Gon's squad proved to be a "different class" as fatigue and injuries caught up with his depleted team.
"We played really, really well in the first half and scored a good goal... but Selangor punished the chances they got," Durakovic said.
"We missed four key players, Endrick dos Santos, Pedro Santos, Rizal Ghazali, and Engku Shakir Engku Yacob.
"If you don't have a big squad, it's not easy to play so many games in so many days. In the second half, we were just tired.
"I tried to give the young boys a chance, but the quality of Selangor is different class. Still, my players gave 100 per cent and I cannot complain."
3341c0b1fe47a345: KUALA LUMPUR: Uzma Bhd's earnings growth is expected to resume in the second quarter (Q2) of financial year 2027 (FY27), as seismic vessel utilisation recovers to above 90 per cent following the completion of dry-docking.

Phillip Capital Sdn Bhd said the recovery would coincide with a gradual pick-up in upstream oil and gas (O&G) activity following Petroliam Nasional Bhd's portfolio optimisation and operatorship realignment in Q1.

It said earnings should gain further traction through full-year contributions from the acquisition of Johnson Pump in December 2025 and a third-party access pipeline gas supply contract secured in Q3 FY26.

Higher contributions from Uzma's new energy business are also expected to support growth, backed by newly secured net energy metering projects. Power generation capacity is expected to ramp up to 150 megawatt (MW)-peak in FY27.
This will be complemented by the commissioning of SARA WIF2.0, which was 85 per cent complete as at end-August and is expected to start contributing from Q3 FY27.

"We gather that tender activity is gaining momentum, with the tender book rising 81 per cent quarter-on-quarter to RM5.6 billion as of June, split 67:33 between non-O&G and O&G," Phillip Capital said.

The firm said Uzma, one of Malaysia's top three Bumiputera solar players, is well positioned to participate in Package 2 of Large Scale Solar 6, which involves 300MW of solar capacity and 150MW of battery energy storage system capacity.
The group is also pursuing several natural gas contracts, each worth about RM100 million annually, as well as an eight-year satellite concession project with the Malaysian government.
"On the O&G front, heightened energy security concerns amid ongoing Middle East tensions are driving increased tender activity for well services projects across Thailand, Vietnam and Myanmar.
"Successful contract wins could provide upside to our FY27 earnings forecasts," Phillip Capital said.
The firm maintained its "Buy" call on Uzma with an unchanged target price of 76 sen.
At current levels, it said Uzma is trading at about three times its estimated FY27 price-to-earnings ratio, which it views as undemanding given the company's strengthening earnings outlook.
4d35ec70908139cb: KUALA LUMPUR: The outlook for Malaysia's semiconductor sector remains constructive, although the recovery is expected to be uneven across subsectors, TA Securities said.

The firm said the sector continued to benefit from structural growth areas, particularly artificial intelligence (AI)-related investments, data centre expansion and demand for advanced semiconductor applications.

"Nevertheless, we expect the recovery to remain uneven across subsectors, with growth likely to be led by integrated circuit design, optoelectronics, and semiconductor packaging and testing, particularly among companies with exposure to AI-related and data centre infrastructure demand.

"In contrast, players with greater exposure to traditional end markets such as personal computers and smartphones may face a more challenging operating environment, partly due to rising memory costs," it said in a note.

TA Securities said the recent US interest rate hike was expected to have a limited direct impact on the earnings of Malaysian semiconductor companies, given the strength of these structural growth drivers.
However, tighter monetary conditions could weigh on valuations, particularly for stocks trading at high multiples.

"This could, however, be partially offset by a potentially stronger US dollar following the rate hike, which would provide some earnings support to export-oriented semiconductor players with US dollar-denominated revenue.
"Overall, we expect the rate hike in the US to have a relatively minimal impact on the local semiconductor sector," it said.
TA Securities said the global semiconductor industry remained firmly in a supercycle, driven by sustained demand from AI-related investments and continued expansion of data centre infrastructure.
Citing the Semiconductor Industry Association, the firm said global semiconductor sales reached US$146.8 billion in July 2026, up 6.4 per cent month-on-month and 135.1 per cent year-on-year (YoY).
This marked the 33rd consecutive month of YoY growth, while cumulative sales for the first seven months of 2026 surged 93.6 per cent to US$784.6 billion.
TA Securities maintained its "Neutral" stance on the semiconductor sector and named Dagang NeXchange Bhd as its top pick, with a target price of 66 sen.
It cited semiconductor subsidiary SilTerra's exposure to the ongoing AI cycle and strong order flows for silicon photonics products amid demand from AI and data centre applications.
The firm also upgraded Unisem M Bhd and Malaysian Pacific Industries Bhd to "Buy" from "Hold", with target prices of RM4.81 and RM47.30, respectively.
It maintained its "Hold" call on Inari Amertron Bhd with a target price of RM2.70.

For Elsoft Research Bhd, TA Securities cut its FY26 to FY28 earnings forecasts by 27.1 per cent, 10.4 per cent and six per cent, respectively, citing lower sales of conventional automated test equipment.
It lowered Elsoft's target price to 25 sen from 28 sen, based on an unchanged 30 times calendar year 2027 price-to-earnings multiple, while maintaining its "Hold" call.
0cfb6eeefe7bef0a: PETALING JAYA: A man and a woman were found dead in a car at Taman Inang Sari in Alor Gajah, Melaka, today.

143cd8dc81e4e195: PETALING JAYA: Keupayaan Najib Razak membayar denda RM50 juta sebagai syarat tahanan rumah sebahagiannya di luar kawalan bekas perdana menteri itu kerana kebanyakan asetnya masih tertakluk kepada perintah pembekuan dan tindakan penguatkuasaan, kata peguamnya.

Di bawah pengampunan bersyarat yang diberikan kepada Najib Jumaat lalu, bekas presiden Umno itu akan menjalani baki hukumannya di bawah tahanan rumah sehingga 23 Ogos 2028, tertakluk kepada pembayaran denda itu.
Firma guaman Shafee & Co dalam kenyataan yang dikeluarkan bagi pihaknya berkata, Najib sedang mempertimbangkan pilihan terbaik untuk memenuhi syarat itu.
Najib masih di Penjara Kajang sementara syarat itu sedang diuruskan dan pasukan guamannya sedang meneliti syarat serta implikasi praktikalnya.

"Sebahagian besar aset, akaun bank dan hartanah anak guam kami masih tertakluk kepada perintah pembekuan dan tindakan penguatkuasaan oleh kerajaan, dan pelupusannya tidak berada dalam kawalan beliau sepenuhnya.
"Oleh itu, keupayaan beliau untuk memenuhi syarat tersebut sebahagiannya bergantung kepada perkara yang berada di luar kawalan beliau."
Peguamnya berkata, Najib berterima kasih kepada mereka yang menawarkan bantuan bagi memenuhi syarat pembayaran denda RM50 juta itu.
Tetapi, katanya, beliau tidak mahu ahli Umno, penyokong atau orang ramai berasa terbeban atau terikat untuk membantunya.
"Beliau tetap berterima kasih kepada mereka yang, atas kerelaan sendiri dan mengikut kemampuan masing-masing, memilih untuk menghulurkan sokongan dan bantuan.
"Keikhlasan mereka merupakan sumber kekuatan amat besar kepada beliau sejak dulu hingga hari ini."
Firma guaman itu berkata, Najib turut menjunjung kasih Yang di-Pertuan Agong, Sultan Ibrahim atas "perkenan baginda melaksanakan kuasa prerogatif pengampunan diraja untuk beliau".
"Anak guam kami menerima keputusan Seri Paduka Baginda dengan penuh kesyukuran dan kerendahan hati."

Najib, 73, diberikan pengampunan bersyarat Jumaat lalu, yang membolehkannya menjalani baki hukuman penjara di bawah tahanan rumah sehingga 23 Ogos 2028, tertakluk kepada pembayaran denda RM50 juta serta syarat lain.

Menurut Bahagian Hal Ehwal Undang-undang Jabatan Perdana Menteri, Najib perlu mematuhi semua syarat ditetapkan dan jika gagal berbuat demikian, pengampunan bersyarat itu akan ditarik balik. Bagaimanapun, tiada butiran syarat diberikan.

Najib mula menjalani hukuman penjara pada Ogos 2022 selepas Mahkamah Persekutuan mengekalkan sabitannya atas kesalahan penyalahgunaan kuasa, pecah amanah dan pengubahan wang haram membabitkan RM42 juta milik SRC International, bekas anak syarikat 1MDB.

Beliau sedang menjalani hukuman di Penjara Kajang selepas Lembaga Pengampunan Wilayah Persekutuan pada Februari 2024 mengurangkan separuh daripada hukuman asalnya selama 12 tahun dan denda RM210 juta kepada RM50 juta.
Yang di-Pertuan Agong mempengerusikan mesyuarat Lembaga Pengampunan Wilayah Persekutuan, yang dianggotai peguam negara, menteri Wilayah Persekutuan dan tiga ahli dilantik baginda.
23e53fcf1d215c48: KUALA LUMPUR, Sept 20 — Former prime minister Datuk Seri Najib Razak’s ability to pay the RM50 million fine required for his house arrest could be complicated by frozen assets, bank accounts and properties subject to government enforcement proceedings, according to his lawyers.

The legal firm Messrs Shafee & Co said a “significant part” of Najib’s assets remained subject to freezing orders and enforcement proceedings, meaning their disposal was not presently within his sole control.
“His ability to satisfy the condition therefore turns in part on matters that do not lie in his own hands,” the lawyers said in a statement issued on Najib’s behalf.
Najib remains at Kajang Prison in the meantime and will only be transferred to house arrest once the conditions are satisfied, the lawyers added.

Attorney General Tan Sri Mohd Dusuki Mokhtar said yesterday that Najib must first pay the RM50 million fine at the Kuala Lumpur High Court Registrar’s Office before the house-arrest process can proceed.

The Federal Territories Pardons Board granted Najib a conditional pardon on Friday, allowing him to serve the remainder of his sentence under house arrest until Aug 23, 2028, subject to the payment and other conditions.

Najib’s lawyers also thanked the King and the Federal Territories Pardons Board for the decision, while Najib expressed gratitude to Deputy Prime Minister and Umno president Datuk Seri Ahmad Zahid Hamidi, the Umno supreme council and the party and Barisan Nasional leadership and members for their support.

Najib has been serving a six-year sentence at Kajang Prison since August 2022 after the Federal Court upheld his conviction in the SRC International case; his original 12-year sentence and RM210 million fine were reduced to six years and RM50 million respectively following a 2024 pardon.
49734313bf198c94: IPOH, Sept 20 — An elderly couple and their grandson were killed in a fire involving a two-storey terraced house at Persiaran Desa Tambun 4, Taman Desa Tambun here early this morning.

“Upon arrival at the scene, the fire and rescue vehicles found that a Class A two-storey terraced house measuring 20 by 70 feet was on fire, with about 70 per cent of the house affected,” she said in a statement today.
Sayani said the 70-year-old male victim was found in the bathroom on the ground floor of the house, while the other two victims were found on the upper floor.
“One victim was found in the upstairs bathroom while another was found in a bedroom near a window on the upper floor of the house,” she said.

She said the fire had been completely extinguished and the operation ended at 8 am today, with all the victims handed over to the police for further action. — Bernama
3b407a6e55b3ebd2: PETALING JAYA: Mayat seorang lelaki dan wanita ditemukan di dalam kereta di Taman Inang Sari, Alor Gajah, Melaka, hari ini.

ebb166aeceb37771: KUALA LUMPUR, Sept 20 — Twenty-two areas nationwide recorded unhealthy Air Pollutant Index (API) readings as of 9am today.

According to the Air Pollutant Index Management System (APIMS) portal, the highest reading was recorded at IPD Serian (182) in Sarawak, while seven areas in the state also recorded unhealthy API readings, namely Samarahan (168), Kuching (166), Sri Aman (163), Bintulu (153), Sibu (152), Sarikei (116) and Samalaju (105).
Five areas in Johor also recorded unhealthy API readings, with Larkin recording 162, Batu Pahat and Pasir Gudang 155 each, followed by Segamat (154) and Tangkak (153).
Meanwhile, Putrajaya and Nilai (Negeri Sembilan) each recorded a reading of 154, while Shah Alam, Selangor recorded 152, followed by Cheras, Kuala Lumpur (133) and Seremban, Negeri Sembilan (127).
Unhealthy API readings were also recorded at Bukit Rambai, Melaka (121), Bandaraya Melaka (114), Johan Setia, Selangor (112) and Petaling Jaya, Selangor (102).
Meanwhile, 40 areas recorded moderate readings, while five areas recorded good readings.
An API reading of zero to 50 indicates good air quality, 51 to 100 (moderate), 101 to 200 (unhealthy), 201 to 300 (very unhealthy) and 301 and above (hazardous).

Meanwhile, Department of Environment (DOE) deputy director-general (Development) Azuri Azizah Saedon, in a statement today, said that the situation was occurring amid persistent dry weather conditions in parts of the southern Asean region.
Based on a report by the Asean Specialised Meteorological Centre (ASMC) yesterday (Sept 19), 865 hotspots were detected in Kalimantan, 16 in Sumatra and six in Malaysia, all in Sarawak.

The ASMC also reported moderate to dense smoke plumes from clusters of hotspots in several areas in Kalimantan and southern Sumatra, with moderate transboundary smoke plumes from Kalimantan moving towards western Sarawak and southern Sabah.
She said haze from southern Sumatra and Kalimantan was also observed moving towards Singapore and southern Peninsular Malaysia.
Meanwhile, DOE said it continued to monitor the risk of fires, particularly in peatland areas and landfill sites that are vulnerable to fires during hot and dry weather.

DOE said monitoring would be stepped up if there was an increase in air pollution, while appropriate action would be taken in accordance with its jurisdiction and legal provisions to minimise the impact on the environment and public health.

“Enforcement action has also been strengthened through inspections and patrols in identified high-risk areas, including agricultural areas, peatlands, plantations, landfill sites and locations with potential for open burning,” the statement said.

DOE also monitors API readings, hotspots and developments in transboundary haze, taking into account meteorological information to assess the situation and coordinate haze management measures at district, state and national levels.
Under the National Haze Action Plan (PTJK), the Disaster Management Committee can be activated by NADMA when the API reading exceeds 150 for more than 24 hours.

The PTJK also stipulates the suspension of outdoor activities when the API reading exceeds 100, the closure of schools, kindergartens and childcare centres when the API reading exceeds 200, while cloud seeding operations may be carried out, subject to the presence of clouds and suitable weather conditions, when the API reading exceeds 150 for more than 24 hours.
The department also urged the public not to carry out open burning, particularly during hot and dry weather and when air quality is at unhealthy to hazardous levels.

It added that under the Environmental Quality (Amendment) Act 2024, offences involving open burning are punishable by a minimum fine of RM25,000 up to RM1 million, or imprisonment for up to five years, or both, while a compound of up to 50 per cent of the maximum fine may also be imposed for each offence.
The public is also urged to report fires or incidents of open burning to the Malaysian Fire and Rescue Department via the 999 emergency line or DOE’s toll-free line at 1-800-88-2727.
“Hourly API readings can be accessed via DOE’s Air Pollutant Index Management System (APIMS) or the official MyJAS EQMS application,” it said. — Bernama
a4acbaeedd56788e: MIRI, Sept 20 — A 10-door longhouse in Kampung Long Jekitan, Ulu Baram, Marudi was completely destroyed in a fire yesterday.
The Sarawak Fire and Rescue Department (Bomba) operation control centre said a distress call was received at about 2.50pm, following which the Marudi Police Station was immediately alerted.

ac4f3c5c71e168a6: PETALING JAYA: Former prime minister Najib Razak’s ability to pay his RM50 million fine imposed as a condition for his house arrest is partly beyond his control as most of his assets remain subject to freezing orders and enforcement proceedings, say his lawyers.

Under the conditional pardon granted to Najib on Friday, the former Umno president will serve the remainder of his sentence in the SRC International case under house arrest until Aug 23, 2028, subject to payment of the fine.
In a statement issued on his behalf today, Messrs Shafee & Co said Najib was considering his options on how best to fulfil the condition.
The law firm said he remained in Kajang prison while the condition was being addressed, and that his legal team was studying the terms of the conditional pardon and their practical implications.

“A significant part of his assets, bank accounts and properties remains subject to freezing orders and enforcement proceedings by the government, and their disposal is not presently within his sole control,” it said.
“His ability to satisfy the condition, therefore, turns in part on matters that do not lie in his own hands.”
The lawyers said Najib also expressed gratitude to those who had offered assistance towards meeting the RM50 million condition.
However, they said, he did not want Umno members, supporters or members of the public to feel burdened or obliged to assist him.
“He remains profoundly grateful to those who, entirely of their own free will and according to their respective means, have chosen to offer their support and assistance,” they said.
“Their kindness is a source of great strength to him at this time.”
The firm said Najib was grateful to the Yang di-Pertuan Agong, Sultan Ibrahim, for “graciously exercising the royal prerogative of mercy in his favour”.
“Our client receives His Majesty’s decision with the utmost humility,” it said.

Najib, 73, was granted a conditional pardon by the Agong on Friday, allowing him to serve the remainder of his prison sentence under house arrest until Aug 23, 2028, subject to payment of his RM50 million fine and other conditions.

The legal affairs division of the Prime Minister’s Department said Najib must comply with all the conditions imposed, failing which the conditional pardon would be revoked. It did not provide details of the conditions.

Najib was imprisoned in August 2022 after the Federal Court upheld his conviction for abuse of power, criminal breach of trust and money laundering involving RM42 million belonging to SRC International, a former subsidiary of 1MDB.

He had been serving a reduced six-year prison sentence at Kajang prison after the Federal Territories Pardons Board halved his original 12-year sentence in February 2024. The initial RM210 million fine was also reduced to RM50 million.
The Agong presides over meetings of the FTPB, which comprises the attorney-general, the federal territories minister, and three members appointed by him.
6ebe060c2a219ecf: SEPTEMBER 20 — As the extended Visit Malaysia 2026-2027 campaign gains momentum, homegrown initiatives are creatively showcasing the nation on a global stage. From urban quests to exotic beach escapades and lofty mountaintop retreats, Malaysia offers an unmatched variety of natural ecosystems waiting to be discovered or perhaps, re-discovered.

Among the nation’s premier draws are its coastal zones and marine biodiversity. However, rapid tourism growth necessitates robust legal safeguards to ensure high-value tourism does not compromise delicate coastal habitats.

Malaysia’s marine biodiversity relies on statutory protections under the Fisheries Act 1985, which designates under Section 41 to Section 45 under Part IX authorised for the establishment of marine parks in Malaysia. By virtue of the divisions of powers under the Federal Constitution, these existing marine parks fall under the federal jurisdictions and are formally institutionalised under the Marine Parks Division under the Department of Fisheries Malaysia, which is a federal agency. Furthermore, mandatory Environmental Impact Assessments (EIAs) under the Environmental Quality Act 1974, particularly Section 34A, ensure that mainland and island resort expansions implement sustainable waste and sewage infrastructure before opening to international visitors.
Action-driven conservation: The Sea Heroes movement
Complementing these statutory protections, public and private NGO partnerships directly engage tourist agencies and creators in environmental stewardship through structured conservation missions:

Coral Ecology and Debris Removal, where it aligned with World Oceans Day 2026, programmes supported by the PADI AWARE Foundation, YBD Dive Centre, YBD Conservation, and Perhentian Marriott Resort & Spa successfully executed underwater cleanups, extracting marine debris and 10 meters of abandoned ghost nets.

The Clean Wave: Scheduled for International Coastal Cleanup Day, this initiative organizers island-wide cleanups, debris classification, and waste data collection to support localized coastal management policy.

Reef Warriors: Focuses on active reef protection through training in Crown-of-Thorns (COTs) starfish identification, population surveying, safe removal techniques, and ongoing ecological impact assessments.
Industry implications: From compliance to competitive advantage
The writers assert that stronger environmental safeguards are needed to protect Malaysia’s marine biodiversity as coastal tourism grows. — Pexels pic

For tourism and hospitality operators, these environmental safeguards are not external constraints but part of the licensing architecture they already work within. The Tourism Industry Act 1992 (Act 482) requires tour operators and travel agencies to be licensed by the Commissioner of Tourism, while Part IV makes it an offence to guide visitors for remuneration without a valid licence.

In marine settings, this matters greatly. The Ministry of Tourism, Arts and Culture (MOTAC) issues a Local Nature Tourist Guide licence tied to specific nature and eco-tourism sites, meaning the person interpreting a coral reef to a diver should be trained in reef ecology rather than merely fluent in storytelling. The same Act governs the registration and star-rating of tourist accommodation premises, giving regulators leverage over island resorts whose wastewater and solid waste directly determine reef water quality. Read alongside Section 34A of the Environmental Quality Act 1974, the operating licence becomes a conservation instrument in its own right.

Hospitality businesses also operate under a parallel set of voluntary standards: the ASEAN Green Hotel Standard, MS ISO 21401 for sustainable management systems, and eco-certification promoted under the National Ecotourism Plan 2016-2025. The National Tourism Policy 2020-2030 positions these as the route to branding Malaysia the “Top of Mind Ecotourism Destination of the World.”

The commercial logic is straightforward. Carrying capacity limits, mooring buoy systems and conservation fees protect the very asset guests pay to see, and a bleached reef yields nothing. Programmes such as Sea Heroes therefore double as product development, converting passive beach stays into certified, high-value experiential packages that command premium rates and longer length of stay.

By pairing enforceable environmental laws with creator-led public awareness, Malaysia establishes a sustainable model for coastal eco-tourism and protecting marine habitats while sharing them with the world.

* Redza Zakaria is the head unit of Maritime Law, Policy and Governance at the Institute of Ocean Earth and Sciences and Senior Lecturer at the Faculty of Law, Universiti Malaya. Mohd Zulfakar Mohd Nawi is a senior lecturer at the Department of Professional Education and Postgraduates, Faculty of Technical and Vocational Education, Universiti Tun Hussein Onn Malaysia.

f11bde9d779954dc: IPOH: An elderly couple and their grandson were killed in a fire at their double-storey terrace house at Taman Desa Tambun here early this morning.
Perak fire and rescue department director Sayani Saidon said personnel from the Tambun and Ipoh stations were deployed to the scene after a call was received at 4am.

She said Raja Ahmad's body was found in the bathroom on the ground floor, and the other two victims were found on the upper floor.
33a31fb4648662fc: IPOH: Sepasang suami isteri dan cucu mereka maut dalam kebakaran sebuah rumah teres dua tingkat di Persiaran Desa Tambun 4, Taman Desa Tambun, di sini.

Pengarah Jabatan Bomba dan Penyelamat (JBPM) Perak, Sayani Saidon, berkata sepasukan anggota dari Balai Bomba dan Penyelamat Tambun serta Ipoh bergegas ke lokasi selepas menerima panggilan 4 pagi tadi.

Beliau berkata, mangsa dikenali Raja Ahmad Raja Ali, 70, Zaitun Mohamed, 64, dan Nik Abdurrahman Azimin Harith Helal, 18, manakala seorang lagi mangsa Raja Ikhwan Hadi Raja Ahmad, 47, selamat kerana dipercayai tidur di ruang parkir rumah itu.
"Setibanya jentera di lokasi kejadian didapati berlaku kebakaran rumah teres dua tingkat jenis kelas A berkeluasan 20 x 70 kaki dan terbakar kira-kira 70%," katanya dalam kenyataan.

32949faab001e9ff: KOTA KINABALU, Sept 20 — Croatian hiker Mauro Persic, who was fined RM25,000 for trespassing into Kinabalu Park, has denied deliberately entering the mountain without permission or trying to avoid paying the entry fee.
The 46-year-old, who lives in London, said his climb was spontaneous and driven by his desire to explore Mount Kinabalu after seeing its beauty firsthand.

“I did not want to trespass nor avoid paying entry fees, that was the last thing on my mind. All I wanted to do was explore the captivating beauty of Kinabalu the moment I saw it,” he said in a Facebook post a day after Malaysia Day.
“As I have done many times before in different places around the globe. I did it on a spur of a moment and did not put enough thought and consideration to it. My sincere apologies for this.”
Persic also apologised to Sabahans who felt he had disrespected them, saying he had no intention of offending the state’s people, culture or the mountain.
“I would like to make an apology to all the people of Sabah who feel that I have disrespected them. I never meant any disrespect to people, culture nor mountain,” he said.
“People of Sabah have treated me like one of their own and I have only words of praise for them.”

Persic said he had also tried to respect the environment during the climb, claiming he left no trace behind and avoided climbing major peaks because of their sacred significance to the Kadazan-Dusun community.

“However, I have been as respectful as ever to the environment, leaving no trace behind and not climbing on top of any major peaks out of respect for sacred meaning that the mountain holds for Kadazan-Dusun people,” he said.
He said he did not consider his climb a conquest of Mount Kinabalu, questioning the idea of “conquering” mountains.
“Lastly, I did not conquer Kinabalu (nor any other mountain for that matter) and I find this commonly quoted concept wrong on so many levels,” he said.
“We might spend a fleeting moment on a peak but the mountain will remain there long after we're gone. Besides, why would one need to conquer anyways?”
Persic’s unauthorised climb came to light on Sept 6 after he sent an SOS when he was injured and stranded on a ledge along a steep slope.
A five-day rescue operation involving 43 personnel eventually brought him to safety, with a porter carrying him down the mountain after rescuers faced steep terrain, rain and poor visibility.
Persic sustained injuries to his right leg and ribs, as well as minor wounds to his hands.
He ended his post with a message for Malaysians: “I wish Happy Malaysia Day to all Malaysians, wherever they might be!”
9a1a053c4f7a0eb8: TOKYO: China's 13-year-old prodigy Yu Zidi and Olympic champion Pan Zhanle cruised through their heats Sunday as swimming got under way on the opening day of the Asian Games.
Yu became the youngest swimming world championships medallist in history last year when she won bronze as a 12-year-old as part of China's 4x200m freestyle relay team.
She also finished a whisker outside the medals in fourth in three world individual events.
She has embellished her growing reputation this year, notably with a victory over multiple American Olympic champion Regan Smith in March.
She opened her Asian Games campaign at the Tokyo Aquatics Centre by breezing through her women's 200m butterfly heat, qualifying for Sunday evening's final with the fastest time in 2min 7.97sec.
It was 2.7sec quicker than the second-fastest qualifier, Chinese compatriot Chang Mohan.
Yu does not turn 14 until October.
Pan was in action in the men's 100m freestyle, the event in which he won gold and set a world record at the Paris Olympics.
He qualified with quickest in 48.07sec, ahead of South Korea's Hwang Sun-woo.
"The first 50 I felt I controlled my speed and then the second 50 I was at the max," said the 22-year-old Pan.
"I think tonight I will be better."
Pan is looking to rebound from a disappointing world championships last year in Singapore, where he failed to make the final in either the 100m or 200m freestyle.
He said his stunning success in Paris had taken time to get used to.
"It's such a big change year by year, especially after Paris. The change is in my training and in my life," he said.
"I'm getting better at adjusting year by year."
Japan's Tomoyuki Matsushita finished fastest in the men's 200m individual medley with a time of 1min 58.56sec.
Japan are looking for better results in the pool after winning only five golds and finishing a distant third in the swimming medals table at the 2023 Asian Games in Hangzhou.
"This is being held in Japan and although there's no pressure, I want to show my best to all the people here," said Matsushita.
86bb7d0d576f4749: NAGOYA, Sept 20 — The first gold medal of the 20th Asian Games was won today by host nation Japan as a 13-year-old swimmer from China started in blistering form on the opening day of the multisports extravaganza.
Japan’s Takumi Hojo won the men’s individual triathlon in Gamagori city near Nagoya with China’s Zhang Xirui second and Kazakhstan’s Arlan Zhanabay taking bronze.
It was the first of 469 gold medals to be awarded at a two-week spectacle that has more athletes than the Olympics.
Action also began in the swimming pool, where Yu Zidi, who does not turn 14 until next month, was fastest by far in the women’s 200m butterfly heats.
Teenager Yu was almost 2.70 seconds quicker than compatriot Chang Mohan and will be a hot favourite to take her first major gold in today evening’s final.
The Games were officially declared open yesterday by Japan’s Emperor Naruhito but there were a large number of empty seats at the 30,000-capacity stadium in Nagoya.
It sounded the starting pistol on two weeks of intense action as the continent’s finest athletes compete in more than 40 sports before the curtain comes down on October 4.
The event in Nagoya and Aichi prefecture has 2028 Olympics places up for grabs but has been dogged by a series of problems in the build-up.
Accommodating the more than 11,000 athletes and 6,000 officials has stretched organisers to the limit after they decided not to have a traditional athletes’ village to save money.
Competitors instead are staying in a combination of temporary container-style huts, hotels and cruise ship the Costa Serena.
There was a record deluge last week which flooded parts of Nagoya and a typhoon is due to skirt the area today night threatening further disruption.
Some athletes were left stranded at the airport when transport failed to turn up and several teams have complained about the quality of the huts, including the beds being too short.
And Games organisers were forced to offer “deepest apologies” after North Korea’s national anthem was played on Friday for South Korea’s men’s hockey team before a preliminary match.
Triathlete Hojo finished the 750m swim, 20km bike ride and 5,000m run in 52min 56sec, nine seconds clear of Zhang with Zhanabay a further six seconds behind in third.
“As it’s our first gold medal, it’s given the Japanese team a real boost,” said the 30-year-old Hojo, whose win will qualify him for the 2028 Olympics in Los Angeles.

“I was really fired-up. Even the rain held off, and I was in top form right up until I stood on the starting line,” added Hojo, who also won the Asian Games test triathlon a year ago on the same course.
“(I knew) it’d be tough, but (I thought) I’ll push myself, and if it works, I think it’ll be a good race.”
As always at the Asian Games — which started in 1951 — Olympic staples such as athletics and swimming will sit side-by-side with regional favourites like sepak takraw and kabaddi.
There will be eSports, breakdancing and BMX cycling. Padel and MMA will make their Asian Games debuts. — AFP
ed05f42d24d06d7f: SIBU, Sept 20 — Sarawak’s annual federal allocation should be determined through a transparent formula rather than decided from year to year, said State Deputy Minister of Public Health, Housing and Local Government Datuk Michael Tiang.
He said such a formula would provide greater certainty over development funding and take into account Sarawak’s contribution to the country’s economy and revenue.

“I fully support our Premier Datuk Patinggi Tan Sri Abang Johari Tun Openg’s suggestion that it is time for the federal government to come up with a formula on how to calculate the annual allocations for Sarawak’s development.
“Have a formula so there is no need to guess every year. The allocation is determined based on how much income and revenue Sarawak generates for Malaysia,” he said.
Tiang said a clear formula would also provide a more transparent and consistent basis for determining how much Sarawak receives each year.
“I think that is fair, transparent and consistent with the principles of democracy.

“We should have a fair share in Malaysia because we formed Malaysia together. Sarawak should be entitled to a fair share based on what we have contributed to the country’s economy, growth and revenue, as well as our share of the nation’s wealth,” he said.

Tiang said the proposed funding formula was one of three key requests he hoped would be considered in the national Budget 2027, alongside the restoration of diesel subsidies and greater state control over public health funding.

Speaking after officiating at the Sibu Division Bodybuilding and Weightlifting Association’s gym grand opening here yesterday, he reiterated the need for what he describes as a transparent, scientific and accountable approach to federal allocations.

On diesel subsidies, Tiang said the current policy had affected commercial operators as well as non-governmental and religious organisations, particularly those providing services between rural and urban areas.
“We hope that the national budget can restore what we had previously for the diesel subsidy. That is my number one plea,” said the Pelawan assemblyman.
He said diesel remained important not only for commercial activities but also for the delivery of government, welfare and other services across Sarawak.
Higher operating costs, he said, could affect the delivery of such services and weaken connectivity between rural and urban communities.

Tiang also noted changes to the Budi Diesel subsidy scheme, including allowing eligible vehicle owners to transfer their subsidy entitlement to a maximum of three vehicles, but said more was needed to address Sarawak’s circumstances.
His other proposal is for the federal government to provide Sarawak with a dedicated public health allocation while giving the state greater discretion over how the funds are distributed and used.
He said this would enable Sarawak to plan and manage its public health resources according to local needs rather than having funding decisions made entirely at the federal level.

“Give the budget to the Sarawak government to decide how to manage the allocation from the federal government. We make our own decision because we know our place well and how to serve our people,” he said. — The Borneo Post
2392ca6fd3be004c: PHILADELPHIA, Sept 20 — Pop star Ed Sheeran said yesterday the situation in Gaza is “unjustifiable,” following a wave of criticism that he had failed to back his opening act who was booted from the tour after making pro-Palestinian comments.
The singer, who had previously maintained an apolitical stance, broke his silence on the Israeli-Palestinian conflict in his first show since the controversy involving US rapper Macklemore.
“What is happening in Gaza is catastrophic and unjustifiable and disproportionate,” Sheeran said in Philadelphia.
“Our hearts have been broken by the scale of devastation and loss of civilians’ lives, children’s lives, and the systemic injustice we’re seeing unfold in the West Bank cannot be overlooked.”
Macklemore had declared “Free Palestine” at a New Jersey concert this month, drawing backlash from owners of US stadiums hosting future dates of Sheeran’s Loop Tour.
The British artist, 35, has denied being behind the decision to remove the rapper, instead blaming the tour promoter.
Four supporting acts subsequently walked out on the Shape of You singer, issuing public statements citing their support for Palestinians.
“I’ve had to take and make difficult decisions, and I am making mistakes, and I’m so so sorry,” an emotional Sheeran told his audience, who responded with cheers.
Sheeran had been accused by critics of failing to stand up to the stadium owners — led by billionaire businessman Robert Kraft — and was targeted by boycott calls.
The singer said he was “deeply worried” about the idea of venues pre-approving the content of performances.
“This happens in so many places that I perform around the world, but it should never happen in the free world.”
Boycott
A few dozen pro-Palestinian protesters rallied peacefully outside Lincoln Financial Field ahead of the concert, waving Palestinian flags and chanting “Free, free Palestine.”
Some of the fans streaming into the stadium said they had hesitated about coming due to the controversy, but ultimately decided to attend and enjoy the music.
But others like Brandon Ateke changed their plans.
The 18-year-old Brown University student accused Sheeran of “complicity” with Kraft and others in silencing Macklemore.
“I decided to not attend the concert and instead attend the protest to bring light to the genocide going on in Gaza today,” he told AFP.
Yesterday, a pro-Palestinian group urged artists, fans and crew members to stay away from Sheeran’s concerts.

“We now extend our call for boycotting Ed Sheeran’s entire world tour, including the upcoming Latin American dates, and the as-yet-unannounced European leg,” the Palestinian Campaign for the Academic and Cultural Boycott of Israel (PACBI) said.
Solo
Sheeran started his show last night alone on stage, without an opening act.
He later brought on five musicians who he said had learned his songs in three days, thanking them for joining him “in a week when no one wants to stand on stage with me.”
The groups that quit the tour included Sheeran’s backing band as well as performer Finneas, who rose to fame collaborating with his pop superstar sister Billie Eilish.

Since Israel invaded Gaza in October 2023 following the worst attack on the country in its history by militant group Hamas, the toll on Palestinians and the wider issue of Palestinian rights have emerged as a rallying cry in the entertainment industry.
From the Oscars to the Emmys, top music awards ceremonies and European film festivals, the Gaza war has frequently pushed its way onto the agenda.

The massive Israeli offensive in Gaza has killed more than 73,800 people, according to the Gaza health ministry, which is under Hamas authority and whose figures are considered reliable by the United Nations.
Yesterday, Gaza authorities said the latest Israeli fire had killed at least four people, including a 10-year-old girl. — AFP
5e6e1bd627cdace2: PETALING JAYA: Kementerian Pendidikan (KPM) akan mengemukakan cadangan kepada Jemaah Menteri untuk menyemak semula struktur pemilikan pusat tuisyen.

"Sehubungan itu, KPM akan mengemukakan cadangan untuk menyemak semula ketetapan berkaitan struktur pemilikan pusat tuisyen untuk pertimbangan Jemaah Menteri minggu depan," katanya dalam kenyataan.

f8fcf522b0d8aa15: AL MAJD: The thunder of hooves and clouds of dust returned to the hills west of Hebron as Palestinians raced Arabian horses through the village of Al-Majd to the cheers of residents.
The annual race in the Israeli-occupied West Bank had been suspended for the past two years in the wake of the Gaza war, but the tradition returned this week, despite ongoing tension.
"Our ambitions are constrained by a lack of financial and logistical resources needed to support the riders, so we simply try to provide whatever we can," said event coordinator Ismael Abu Awad.
After the starting gun was fired, the riders set off along the winding dirt track cutting through the rocky landscape, while spectators cheered the course and on rooftops.
The competition culminated in jubilant celebrations, with supporters surrounding the winning jockey and lifting trophies above the crowd.
Arabian horses occupy a special place in Palestinian culture, and horse races and equestrian beauty championships are held across the West Bank, drawing competitors from different towns and villages.
Open land has become becomes increasingly scarce amid expanding Israeli settlement construction in the West Bank, occupied since 1967.
But horse culture still draws Palestinians together, from urban neighbourhoods to rural villages.

For the local community, Friday's race was more than just about sports. It was aimed at "preserving a form of Arab heritage that our ancestors cherished and that we continue to uphold today," Abu Awad told AFP.
The event also provided an opportunity for local jockeys who cannot easily participate in international races to showcase their skills, the organiser said.
"Some horses and riders face difficulties travelling to Jordan or abroad," he said.
Despite the challenges, participants spoke of dreams that stretch beyond the local track.
"My ambition is to travel to Italy to ride horses," said racer Mohammed Al-Ajlouni. "We ride here now, but for the future, that is what I hope for."
0cd9da511ac4d616: PETALING JAYA: The Malaysian Employers Federation (MEF) has welcomed a one-off RM1,000 mobility assistance allowance for Social Security Organisation (Perkeso) contributors who secure jobs more than 100km from home, but said accessibility and timely delivery are key to its success.
The initiative, announced by human resources minister R Ramanan, will take effect from Oct 1 through amendments to the Employment Insurance System (EIS) Act 2017.

MEF senior adviser for government, media and international engagement Syed Hussain Syed Husman said the allowance could help overcome geographical barriers to employment and improve the matching of workers with vacancies.

“Employment opportunities do not always arise within commuting distance of a worker’s home. The one-off RM1,000 allowance recognises that relocation and extended travel may involve genuine upfront costs,” he said in a statement.
Syed Hussain urged Perkeso to ensure eligible workers were clearly informed about the scheme and could apply through a straightforward and transparent process.

“The success of any employment incentive ultimately depends on accessibility, awareness, and timely delivery,” he said, adding that Perkeso should clearly communicate the eligibility criteria, application procedures, and payment timelines.

Syed Hussain also welcomed other EIS enhancements, including raising the early re-employment allowance from 25% to 50% of the remaining unpaid job search allowance for eligible workers who return to work.
The daily training allowance will also increase to RM30 from RM10-RM20, while the maximum training fee covered will rise from RM4,000 to RM7,000.
He said the measures would help workers move to where jobs were available, acquire new skills, and transition into different occupations.
He also said the government should track the take-up and outcomes of the mobility allowance, including the jobs secured, and whether recipients remained employed.
The data would help determine whether the programme was meeting its objective, and guide future improvements to employment support.
e4d0783709bc9738: KUANTAN, Sept 20 — A mother has removed her 14-year-old son from a religious secondary school in Rompin after he was allegedly assaulted by senior students at a hostel last week, Harian Metro reported.

The 40-year-old entrepreneur said she was also upset that school authorities allegedly failed to take action despite being informed about the incident, prompting her to lodge a police report and arrange to transfer her son to another school.

“I decided to go straight to the school and when I arrived at the hostel, I was shocked to see my son’s body and hands covered in bruises. The senior students allegedly involved in the incident were free to move around,” she told reporters at her home in Bukit Rangin here yesterday.

The woman said the incident happened on September 12 when five senior students allegedly called her son and a friend to their hostel room at about midnight and reprimanded them for leaving the school grounds without permission.
She alleged that the students then blindfolded her son before punching him in the stomach, kicking his back, slapping his face and hitting him with a broomstick.
“They mistreated him for more than an hour and threatened to hurt him with a folding knife and a piece of glass,” she said.
She said her son reported the incident to the school management but no action was taken.
The woman said her son later contacted his father from a public telephone on Sept 16 after learning that the senior students were allegedly planning another attack.
She said that when she contacted the hostel warden, she was told not to come to the school as the matter had already been resolved.
“I then lodged a police report on September 17 and took my son to hospital for an examination,” she said.
The mother of two said she was later told by other parents that several students had allegedly been assaulted by senior students previously, but the incidents had never been disclosed by the school.
She said her son had been left to treat his injuries himself and that she was relieved he had survived the alleged assault.
Fearing for his safety, she told him to pack his belongings on Sept 16 and is now arranging for him to transfer to another school.

Harian Metro also reported Rompin deputy police chief Deputy Superintendent Mohamad Zamri Mohamad Zaber saying that five students have been detained after two victims lodged separate reports at about 1pm on September 17.
He said the suspects comprised three Form Five students and two Form Four students, and all had been questioned to assist investigations under Section 147 of the Penal Code for rioting.
The offence carries a maximum two-year jail term, a fine, or both, upon conviction.
“Both victims sustained injuries believed to have been caused by the attack. All the suspects have been released on police bail,” he was quoted as saying.

5e28fc85eec318e6: KUALA LUMPUR, Sept 20 — The Prisons Department is expected to issue standard operating procedures (SOPs) for Datuk Seri Najib Razak’s house arrest soon, with the rules to cover visits, security and monitoring of the former prime minister’s movements.

Attorney General Tan Sri Mohd Dusuki Mokhtar said, however, that Najib must first pay the RM50 million fine at the Kuala Lumpur High Court Registrar’s Office before the house arrest process can proceed, The Star reported today.

“I understand that there will be an SOP issued for the purpose of house arrest. He would first have to pay the RM50mil fine at the Kuala Lumpur High Court Registrar’s Office before the house arrest process could proceed,” Dusuki was quoted as saying.
Yesterday, reporters camped outside Najib’s home at Jalan Langgak Duta observed a team of Prisons Department personnel passing through the gate in the morning, and exiting a few hours later.
Several police vehicles were also seen arriving at the house throughout the day, with some personnel entering the residence, although the purpose of their visits was not immediately known.

The developments follow the Prime Minister’s Department’s announcement on Friday that Najib had been granted a conditional pardon allowing him to serve the remainder of his sentence under house arrest until August 23, 2028.

The pardon was granted at the 64th meeting of the Federal Territories Pardons Board, chaired by His Majesty Sultan Ibrahim, King of Malaysia, and is subject to conditions including settlement of the RM50 million fine.

Najib’s house arrest arrangement follows his conviction in the SRC International case, for which he has been serving a prison sentence since August 2022 after the Federal Court upheld his conviction on seven charges involving RM42 million belonging to SRC International.

31fed871e382cf10: Reactions to former prime minister Najib Razak’s conditional pardon have come in fast and furious, with some singling out Pakatan Harapan and DAP’s Hannah Yeoh for abandoning their stance on graft.

Yeoh, as the federal territories minister, sits on the Federal Territories Pardons Board that met on Friday morning. The Yang di-Pertuan Agong, Sultan Ibrahim, who presides over the meeting, granted Najib the conditional pardon, according to the legal affairs division of the Prime Ministers' Department.
But before we, the general public, turn into keyboard warriors waiting to pounce on what we deem to be a gross injustice, there are a few things to bear in mind.

First, Najib did not obtain a full pardon. Umno was pushing for it, but Sultan Ibrahim, in his wisdom, thought otherwise. Najib still has to serve his reduced sentence, at home, once he pays RM50 million up front.
This decision is extremely fair when considering that Najib could have received a full pardon like the one obtained by Anwar Ibrahim in 2018.
Second, the conditional pardon is for the conviction in the SRC International case, not for the 1MDB case. This means Najib isn’t going galavanting any time soon.
Third — and this cannot be emphasised enough -- the power to grant pardons lies with the King and not any sitting government.

Yes, government representatives sit on the pardons board, and that is all we know. We will never know what is discussed, as the minutes of the meeting are classified under the Official Secrets Act. And because we don’t know the discussions that took place, it would be unwise to make assumptions.
It is for this very reason we should not be pointing fingers at the government or Yeoh. The King makes his decision based on the discussions held. End of story.
With these three things out of the way, Najib’s conditional pardon however raises two concerns.
One: does house arrest mean he would be able to receive visitors? Would he have access to social media? Access which would allow him to plan his political comeback?
It doesn't sit right with me if Najib is allowed to receive visitors or access to social media. Irrespective of who you are, the rules and regulations of a house arrest should apply equally.
Two: there will no doubt be politicians who want to resign from government because of Najib’s conditional pardon.
Principled maybe, but not necessarily right. Such a sharp response could be construed as defiance of the King’s will. A move that would undoubtedly whip up a racial and religious rhetoric.
So stay on. And if you need to voice your grievances do so politely. The same goes for those who want to hold demonstrations. Don’ go overboard as it would only sully the royal institution.

Politicians being placed under house arrest isn’t a new phenomenon in the world. Prominent figures in other countries have undergone a similar sentence. Najib only has the “honour” of being the first in Malaysia.
Mind you, he wasn’t pardoned for his crimes, and as a citizen I can live with that.
The views expressed are those of the writer and do not necessarily reflect those of FMT.
